title: Latin America
summary: Latin America is used for the area south of the Rio Grande collectively (or three or more of its regions) and as the collective heading/subdivision for its Spanish-speaking countries. Latin Americans covers citizens of Latin American countries collectively; Spanish Americans (Latin America) covers Spanish-speaking ones; Hispanic Americans covers U.S. citizens of Latin American descent. The adjective Latin American qualifies headings for material collectively about Spanish, Portuguese, English and/or French-speaking Latin America; Spanish American qualifies literary headings limited to Spanish-speaking parts.
validation_rules: Assign `Latin America` to works dealing collectively with the area and/or countries south of the Rio Grande, or with all or parts of three or more of its regions (Mexico, Central America, South America, the West Indies). (H 985 sec. 1)
Use `Latin America` as the collective geographic heading and subdivision for the Spanish-speaking countries of Latin America. (H 985 sec. 1)
Use `Latin Americans` for works dealing collectively with citizens of Latin American countries. (H 985 sec. 2)
For works limited to Spanish-speaking Latin Americans, use `Spanish Americans (Latin America)`. (H 985 sec. 2)
Use `Hispanic Americans` (not `Latin Americans`) for United States citizens of Latin American descent. (H 985 sec. 2)

Headings with the adjective `Latin American` designate origin or occurrence in Latin America and are constructed per H 320 and H 351, e.g. `Arts, Latin American`, `National characteristics, Latin American`, `United States--Foreign public opinion, Latin American`. (H 985 sec. 3)

Use `Latin American` to qualify literary headings for material relating collectively to the Spanish, Portuguese, English, and/or French-speaking countries of Latin America, e.g. `Authors, Latin American`, `Love poetry, Latin American`, `Latin American fiction`. (H 985 sec. 3)

Use `Spanish American` to qualify literary headings for material limited to the parts of Latin America where Spanish prevails, e.g. `Spanish American poetry`, `Women authors, Spanish American`, `Historical fiction, Spanish American`. (H 985 sec. 4)

sections.heading: BACKGROUND
sections.text: This instruction sheet provides guidelines for assigning the subject headings Latin America and Latin Americans and for constructing and assigning headings incorporating the adjectives Latin American and Spanish American.

sections.heading: 1. Latin America
sections.text:
Assign the heading Latin America to works dealing collectively with the area and/or countries south of the Rio Grande, as well as all or parts of three or more of the regions that make up Latin America, that is, Mexico, Central America, South America, and the West Indies.

Also assign Latin America as the collective geographic heading and subdivision for the Spanish-speaking countries of Latin America.

sections.heading: 2. Latin Americans
sections.text:
Assign the heading Latin Americans to works dealing collectively with the citizens of Latin American countries. For works limited to Spanish-speaking Latin Americans, use Spanish Americans (Latin America).

Use the heading Hispanic Americans for United States citizens of Latin American descent.

sections.heading: 3. Latin American
sections.text:
Construct and assign headings incorporating the adjective Latin American in accordance with the provisions of H 320 and H 351 to designate origin or occurrence in Latin America. Examples:

```
650 #0 $a Arts, Latin American.
650 #0 $a National characteristics, Latin American.
651 #0 $a United States $x Foreign public opinion, Latin American.
```

Use Latin American to qualify literary subject headings referring to material relating collectively to the Spanish, Portuguese, English, and/or French-speaking countries of Latin America. Examples:

```
650 #0 $a Authors, Latin American.
650 #0 $a Love poetry, Latin American.
650 #0 $a Latin American fiction.
```

sections.heading: 4. Spanish American
sections.text:
Qualify literary subject headings with the adjective Spanish American to refer to material limited to the parts of Latin America where Spanish is the prevailing language. Examples:

```
650 #0 $a Spanish American poetry.
650 #0 $a Women authors, Spanish American.
650 #0 $a Historical fiction, Spanish American.
```
